title.en: To the Tune Shuidiao Getou: How Long Has the Bright Moon Been There

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource; the variant readings it marks are left out.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，删去其所注异文。

basis.en: Song dynasty lyric (ci); the author died in 1101.

note.en: Written at Mid-Autumn 1076 in Mizhou, when Su Shi had not seen his brother Ziyou, Su Zhe, for several years; his preface says he drank until dawn and wrote it thinking of him. It begins by borrowing Li Bai's question to the moon and ends on one of the best-loved wishes in Chinese: that we live long, and share the same moonlight across a thousand li. Notice that the poet weighs the cold palace in the sky against the human world, and chooses the world.
note.zh: 1076 年中秋作于密州，当时苏轼已经几年没有见到弟弟子由（苏辙），词前小序说是欢饮达旦、大醉之后“兼怀子由”而作。开头借用李白问月，结尾是汉语里最受喜爱的祝愿之一：但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。留意他把天上的琼楼玉宇与人间放在一起掂量，最后选了人间。

excerpt.orig: 但願人長久，千里共嬋娟。
excerpt.en: I only wish that we may both live long / and share, a thousand li apart, the beauty of the moon.
excerpt.zh: 但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。
